implementation_statement: Access control policy POL-02 (2024) was revised and approved 2026-09-17, effective 2026-10-01 (P06). Procedures for quarterly access reviews and plant floor accounts are being written.

Workforce accounts are provisioned in the identity provider from the HR feed and federated to the landing zone, PLM, eQMS, repositories, and the CCC admin plane. Terminations disable identity provider access automatically. Gaps: access reviews are annual (last January 2026), not quarterly; MES and test station operator accounts are shared and outside the identity provider (gap 5); P07 found 4 of 25 sampled transfers kept prior repository or cloud roles.
evidence: HR feed configuration; identity provider export; access review January 2026

implementation_statement: Account creation, disablement, and removal run automatically from HR events through the identity provider workflow for all federated systems.
The identity provider disables accounts after 45 days of inactivity. Gap: local accounts on MES terminals, test stations, and the factory provisioning server are not covered.
evidence: Inactivity policy; local account listing from 10 stations

provider_if_inherited: CCC application (company code); Cloud provider (SOC 2 Type 2)
implementation_statement: Hospital users are confined to their own tenant by application and database row-level controls; company support roles are read-only by default. Cloud permissions come from directory groups. Gap: 9 site reliability engineers hold standing write access to production across all tenants (gap 7).
evidence: Role matrix; tenant isolation test results (2025 penetration test); permission set export

implementation_statement: Cloud traffic between accounts passes the shared network hub and cloud firewall; the CCC has no inbound path except the device gateway and the web front end. Plant: a firewall separates the office and OT networks, but Line 1 and Line 3 share one flat OT segment and a vendor VPN appliance terminates inside it (gap 4).
evidence: Firewall rule exports; plant network diagram (2026-07); walkthrough 2026-08-18

implementation_statement: Release signing needs two approvers (a release engineer and a product security engineer). Production deployment approvals are separate from code authors. Gap: 3 controls engineers can both change test station scripts and release them to the line without a second reviewer.
evidence: Signing approval logs; pipeline approval rules; MES change log

implementation_statement: Least privilege is enforced through role groups in the identity provider and cloud permission sets. Gaps: standing all-tenant production write access (9 engineers); 22 engineers hold administrator rights on build runners; plant technicians use local administrator rights on test stations.
evidence: Permission set export; runner admin list; P07 AC-6 results

implementation_statement: Administrators use separate privileged accounts for cloud, identity, and repository administration; daily work uses non-privileged accounts.

Privileged cloud roles are limited to named engineers; the database uses just-in-time elevation through the privileged access broker. Gap: just-in-time access does not yet cover the container platform, the build and signing account, or the identity provider.
evidence: Privileged access broker logs; permission set export

implementation_statement: The identity provider locks accounts after 10 failed attempts and applies risk-based sign-in rules; hospital portal accounts lock after 5 failed attempts.

Workforce remote access uses the identity provider with MFA and device compliance checks; administrative sessions to cloud workloads go through the access broker. Gap: a line equipment vendor has a persistent VPN appliance into the plant OT network with a shared account (gap 4).
evidence: Conditional access policies; vendor VPN appliance configuration

implementation_statement: Corporate wireless uses certificate-based enterprise authentication; the plant has no wireless access into the OT network; guest wireless is isolated.
Awareness and training requirements are in POL-01 and POL-05 (2024, revised 2026-09-17).

All workforce complete annual awareness training (97% completion for 2026); monthly phishing simulations (June 2026 click rate 5.9%). Plant operators receive a short floor version covering USB media and reporting.

Firmware and cloud engineers complete annual secure coding training. Gaps: no role-based training for controls engineers on OT security, or for complaint handlers on recognizing cybersecurity signals for MDR decisions.
evidence: Secure coding training records; complaint handler curriculum

implementation_statement: Logging requirements are in POL-03 and the draft logging and monitoring standard STD-02 (due 2026-12-31).

Cloud control-plane, identity provider, CCC application, database audit, and EDR events are logged. Gaps: MES, test stations, the provisioning server, PLM, and the build pipeline do not send events to the SIEM (gap 8); device security events from VM-7 and IP-4 are kept on the device only.
evidence: Log source list in the SIEM; STD-02 draft

control_name: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
implementation_statement: The MSSP reviews SIEM alerts 24x7 and calls the Security Manager within 30 minutes on high severity. Gap: no routine review of CCC privileged activity or bulk PHI exports; no review of signing service logs.
Automated correlation of CCC privileged activity and PHI export events with the SIEM is planned with STD-02 (due 2027-01-31).
Cloud audit logs from all accounts land in a write-once bucket in the security and log archive account; only 2 security staff can read it and no one can delete it before retention ends.

Cloud audit logs are kept 1 year in the archive. CCC application logs are kept 90 days. Gap: plant and MES logs roll over locally in days; retention for investigations and FDA records questions is not defined in a standard.
Audit record generation is enabled on cloud services, the database, and the CCC application. Gap: plant OT assets and the provisioning server do not generate centrally collected records.
An independent assessment of the DLP is performed annually by the co-sourced internal audit firm, which does not operate any assessed control (P07, 2026-08-10 to 2026-08-28).

Interfaces with hospital EHRs, clinical communication systems, and identity providers are defined in the BAAs and interface specifications. Gap: 31 hospital site-to-site VPNs have no written interconnection security terms.
A POA&M tracks every weakness from P03 and P07 with owners and dates; the vCISO reports status to the audit committee each quarter.
The COO accepted operation of the DLP with conditions on 2026-09-17 (SSP section 4.2); the CEO accepts High risks.

Cloud posture management scores all accounts continuously; monthly vulnerability and posture reports go to the IT Director and Product Security Manager. Gaps: no continuous monitoring of plant OT; TPLC security metrics tracked only for VM-7 (gap 2).

Selected by tailoring (not in the Moderate baseline): independent penetration tests of VM-7, IP-4, and the CCC each year, with tester independence as FDA's premarket guidance recommends (last tests 2025; 2026 tests contracted for 2026-10).
evidence: 2025 penetration test reports; 2026 statement of work

implementation_statement: Configuration management requirements are in POL-01; the configuration standard STD-01 and OT security standard STD-04 are drafts (gap 14).

CCC infrastructure is defined as code and deployed from the pipeline; container images are built from approved base images. Gaps: no documented baselines for test stations, MES servers, and line PLC programs; golden images exist for only 2 of 5 test station types.
evidence: Infrastructure code repository; base image list; plant walkthrough

implementation_statement: Product and CCC changes follow design change control with a cybersecurity impact question (added 2025). Gaps: 5 of 20 sampled product changes skipped the question; plant equipment and test station script changes follow a separate maintenance log with no security review or revalidation trigger (gap 12). This gap allowed R-049.
evidence: Change records sample (P07); MES maintenance log

implementation_statement: Design changes get a documented impact analysis, including whether a new submission is needed and whether the change affects cybersecurity (FDA premarket guidance section VII.D). Gap: test station changes get no impact analysis.
Branch protection requires reviewed merges; pipeline service accounts deploy to production. Gap: test station scripts are edited directly on the stations by controls engineers.

Organization guardrails block public storage, unencrypted volumes, and unapproved regions; container images are scanned against benchmark settings. Gaps: no benchmark scans of Windows servers in the plant; MES terminals have no hardening standard.
Device images disable unused services and ports by default. Gap: P07 found IP-4 pumps shipped with the factory service mode left enabled after final test (R-049).
evidence: Device hardening checklist; P07 lab test 2026-08-19

implementation_statement: IT and cloud asset inventories are automated. Gaps: the OT asset inventory is about 70% complete (gap 4); the VM-5 has no SBOM (gap 1).
evidence: Asset inventory exports; OT inventory spreadsheet

implementation_statement: Users cannot install software on managed endpoints without an approved catalog request; test stations are locked by the application whitelist on 41 of 52 stations.

Selected by tailoring: VM-7, IP-4, and AI-001 verify firmware and model signatures at boot and before install; CCC containers are signed and verified at deployment. VM-5 checks signatures but has no secure boot.
evidence: Secure boot test records; admission policy

implementation_statement: Contingency requirements are in POL-03; the contingency and recovery standard STD-07 is a draft due 2026-12-31.

A CCC contingency plan exists (2025) with BIA recovery objectives (P05). Gaps: no contingency plans for the build and signing pipeline, the MES, or the provisioning server; the plan does not cover HSM key recovery.
The CCC contingency plan is coordinated with hospital downtime procedures in the customer security guide. Gap: not coordinated with the plant emergency plan or supplier continuity.
evidence: Customer security guide; plant emergency plan

implementation_statement: Contingency training for site reliability engineers and plant supervisors is planned after STD-07 is issued (first session 2027-02).
The CCC regional failover test was run once (2025) and took 6 hours against a 2-hour RTO. No tests of the MES, build pipeline, or key recovery (gap 11).
Backups are stored in a separate backup account in a second region with write-once retention.
A second region is provisioned for the CCC with the infrastructure code. Gap: failover is manual and exceeds the RTO.

The CCC database has point-in-time recovery (5-minute log interval) and daily write-once snapshots (35 days) in the backup account with separate administrator credentials. Gap: the MES database is backed up nightly to a plant file server on the same OT network only.
evidence: Backup job reports (30 of 30 days, July 2026); MES backup log

implementation_statement: CCC backups are restored monthly into non-production to test integrity. Gap: MES backups have never been test-restored.

The CCC can be rebuilt from infrastructure code and restored to a point in time. Gaps: recovery of HSM-held signing keys and the VM-5 legacy key has never been exercised; plant station rebuild relies on golden images for only 2 of 5 station types.
Identification and authentication rules are in POL-02 and the authenticator standard STD-06.
Every workforce user has a unique identity in the identity provider. Gap: MES terminals and test stations use shared operator logins (gap 5).
evidence: Identity provider export; MES account list

implementation_statement: Privileged accounts use phishing-resistant hardware keys enforced by the identity provider.
evidence: Conditional access policy; P07 sign-in test

implementation_statement: All non-privileged workforce accounts use push MFA with number matching. Gap: plant floor stations have no MFA.
VM-7 and IP-4 authenticate to the CCC with unique per-device certificates (mutual TLS). Gap: VM-5 uses a per-hospital shared API key (gap 3).

Authenticator rules follow STD-06 (14-character minimum, banned list). Gaps: shared operator passwords on MES and test stations are not changed when staff leave; the vendor VPN account password is shared; the IP-4 factory service credential was the same on every pump that left service mode enabled (R-049).
Device certificates chain to a private certificate authority whose root is offline in the HSM. Gap: the factory provisioning server holds the issuing intermediate key in software (gap 6).
evidence: Certificate authority design; provisioning server walkthrough

implementation_statement: Clinicians sign in through their hospital's identity provider (federation for 212 hospitals) or local portal accounts with MFA.
POL-03 was revised 2026-09-17 to cover product security incidents and integrate PSIRT, MDR, and correction decisions; procedures are in P08.
Incident handlers and the PSIRT receive annual training. Gap: complaint handlers and field service engineers have no training on product security signals.
A corporate ransomware tabletop was held in 2025. Gap: no exercise combining a product vulnerability, FDA decisions, and business associate notice (gap 9). Combined tabletop scheduled 2026-11-12.

Corporate incidents are handled by the Security Manager with the MSSP; product incidents by the PSIRT. Gap: the two processes had separate severity scales and no shared crisis management path until the 2026-09-17 revision (P08).
All security and product security incidents are logged and tracked to closure, with discovery dates recorded.

Staff report incidents through the service desk security line; the VP QA/RA decides MDR and 806 reports; the Compliance and Privacy Officer decides business associate notices. Gap: notice terms in 290 BAAs are not tracked in one register (gap 9).
The MSSP provides 24x7 response support; the cyber insurer's panel provides breach counsel and forensics; the ISAO provides threat and vulnerability sharing.
evidence: MSSP contract; insurance policy; ISAO membership

implementation_statement: The corporate plan and PSIRT procedure are joined by the P08 runbooks approved 2026-09-17. Gap: not yet exercised.
Plant equipment maintenance is scheduled and logged in the MES. Gap: maintenance by line equipment vendors is not supervised when done remotely.

CCC administrative sessions go through the access broker with session recording. Gap: the line equipment vendor connects through its own persistent VPN appliance without session approval or recording.
evidence: Access broker logs; vendor VPN configuration

implementation_statement: Returned devices are wiped of patient data at the Line 4 depot using a documented procedure before refurbishment. Gap: no sanitization records for engineering lab test devices returned from hospital pilots.
Badge access for the plant, labs, and server rooms is approved by area owners and reviewed quarterly.
The campus has staffed reception, badge readers on all plant and lab doors, and a locked server room; visitors are escorted.
Visitor logs are kept at reception for 2 years; engineering labs and the plant require escorts.
Planning policy is part of POL-01; the SSP is reviewed annually.
This SSP describes the DLP; approved 2026-09-17.
POL-05 acceptable use (rules of behavior) is acknowledged at hire and annually (96% for 2026).

Security architecture views (global system, multi-patient harm, updatability and patchability, security use cases) exist for VM-7, IP-4, and AI-001 as FDA's premarket guidance recommends. Gap: no architecture view of the plant provisioning path, which is part of how devices get their identities.
Selected by tailoring: the security program is documented in POL-01, this SSP, and the roadmap in P03. Gap: product security and enterprise security plans were separate until 2026.
Selected by tailoring: the IT Director is designated HIPAA security official for the CCC; the VP QA/RA owns section 524B compliance; the vCISO leads program strategy.
Selected by tailoring: risk appetite statements and acceptance authorities approved by the CEO 2026-09-17 (P01).

control_name: Security and Privacy Groups and Associations
implementation_statement: Selected by tailoring: active member of a health sector ISAO since 2024; the PSIRT shares customer communications with the ISAO, which is one of FDA's enforcement-discretion conditions.
HR terminations disable identity provider access the same day (25 of 25 sampled). Gaps: shared plant operator passwords are not changed at departure; badge removal is manual.
Transfers trigger a manager access review. Gap: 4 of 25 sampled transfers kept prior repository or cloud roles.
Contractors and vendors sign confidentiality terms and, where they touch PHI, subcontractor BAAs. Gap: 2 of 18 PHI subcontractors have no BAA (gap 10).
A sanctions procedure applies to security and privacy violations; sanctions are documented by HR and the Compliance and Privacy Officer.
Risk assessment requirements are in POL-01 (SP 800-30 method, annual cycle).
The DLP is categorized Moderate under FIPS 199 (SSP section 6).
The enterprise risk assessment was completed 2026-07-31 using SP 800-30 Rev. 1 (P01, 50 risks); device threat models and cybersecurity risk assessments are maintained per product in PLM.
Software components are assessed through SBOMs and vulnerability matching. Gap: critical software suppliers are not assessed, and 6 of 22 have no vulnerability notification terms (gap 10).

Cloud workloads are scanned monthly with authentication; SBOMs are matched daily against vulnerability databases. Gaps: 41 matched component vulnerabilities older than 90 days lack an exploitability assessment; KEV matching is manual and weekly; no scanning of plant OT (gap 1, gap 4).
A published CVD policy invites reports to security@ with a 3-business-day acknowledgment target (13 of 14 reports in 2026 met it).
Risk responses are recorded in P01 and the POA&M. Gap: product vulnerability risk decisions are recorded in PLM, separate from the enterprise register.
The BIA identifies critical processes (P05). Gap: no component-level criticality analysis of the provisioning and signing paths.
The SPDF procedure (2025) defines security activities in each phase of device and CCC development under QMSR design controls.
Purchase of software components and line equipment uses supplier qualification. Gap: security requirements are not in purchase specifications for line equipment and test systems.
Security design principles (least privilege, defense in depth, secure defaults, fail-safe alarms) are applied and documented in the architecture views.

External services are covered by contracts and, for PHI, subcontractor BAAs; SOC 2 reports are reviewed for Tier 1 vendors (P09). Gap: 2 PHI subcontractors without BAAs; the line equipment vendor's remote access is outside any agreement on security.
Source code, builds, and releases are version-controlled; every release is traced from commit to signed artifact to SBOM.

Static analysis, software composition analysis, and fuzzing of the device gateway run in CI; independent penetration tests yearly (CA-8). Gap: security review of unresolved anomalies is not recorded for IP-4 releases.
The SPDF and coding standards define approved tools, languages, and review requirements for device and cloud code.

Component support status and end-of-support dates are recorded in the SBOMs for current products. Gaps: VM-5 embedded OS end of support in 2027-06 with no customer plan (gap 3); 11 test stations run an unsupported operating system (gap 4).
evidence: SBOM support fields; test station inventory

implementation_statement: The device gateway and web front end sit behind the provider's denial-of-service protection and a web application firewall with rate limits.

The landing zone routes all traffic through the network hub and cloud firewall; the CCC has no other inbound paths. Plant: office and OT are separated by a firewall, but Line 1 and Line 3 share one segment and the vendor VPN lands inside it (gap 4).

control_name: Deny by Default — Allow by Exception
implementation_statement: Cloud security groups deny by default. Gap: the plant OT firewall has 14 broad allow rules between office and OT networks.
All CCC interfaces use TLS 1.2 or higher; devices use mutual TLS (VM-7, IP-4) or TLS (VM-5); HL7 flows use TLS or site-to-site VPN.

Data keys are managed in the cloud key service; release signing keys and the device CA root are in the HSM with dual control. Gaps: the provisioning server's issuing key is in software (gap 6); the VM-5 legacy signing key is on an offline laptop (gap 3).
Approved algorithms per STD-08; validated cryptographic modules in the cloud services and HSM.
A private PKI issues device and service certificates under a certificate policy. Gap: certificate revocation for compromised devices is manual.
CCC databases, object storage, and backups are encrypted at rest with company-managed keys; laptops use full-disk encryption.

CCC components are patched through image rebuilds (critical within 14 days). Gaps: the IP-4 release cycle is semiannual and 38% of IP-4 pumps run firmware more than two releases old (gap 2); test stations and MES servers are patched quarterly at best.
evidence: Patch reports; release history; adoption data

implementation_statement: EDR runs on all IT endpoints and cloud virtual machines with 24x7 MSSP response. Test stations use application allowlisting instead (41 of 52).
The MSSP monitors IT, identity, and cloud events. Gap: no monitoring of plant OT traffic, the MES, the provisioning server, or the build pipeline (gap 8).
The PSIRT receives ISAO, CISA, and supplier advisories. Gap: advisories for plant equipment and OT software go to nobody in particular.
Firmware, AI-001 model files, and containers are signed and verified; the CCC database uses integrity constraints and audit trails; drug library files are signed by the pharmacist's approval step.
evidence: Signature verification tests; drug library workflow

implementation_statement: Selected by tailoring: devices authenticate code with the release signature before install; VM-5 verifies signatures without secure boot.
evidence: Secure boot and update test records

implementation_statement: Device and interface inputs are validated (schema validation on HL7 and FHIR, range checks on pump programming orders).
Complaint, MDR, and correction records follow QMSR retention; security records are kept 6 years (164.316). Gap: CVD and PSIRT records are not in the records retention schedule.
A supply chain risk management plan covering software components, line equipment, and contract suppliers is planned for 2027-03-31.

SBOMs identify commercial, open-source, and off-the-shelf components for current products; components are pulled from an internal mirror. Gap: no SBOM for VM-5; no provenance checks on line equipment software.
Security terms (vulnerability notification within 30 days, support dates, SBOM delivery) will be added to software supplier contracts at renewal from 2026-12.
Tier 1 vendors are reviewed yearly through SOC 2 reports (P09). Gap: critical software component suppliers and line equipment vendors are not assessed.
Component authenticity checks (authorized distributors, incoming inspection of programmable parts) are being extended to programmable components; procedure due 2027-03-31.
